verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew and the Orion spacecraft safely returned to Earth on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA’s Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down... on Friday, April 10'; R3: 'splashed down on April 10, 2026'; R4: 'SPLASHDOWN! ... back on Earth ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)'; R9: 'splashed down at 5:07 p.m. PDT Friday off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm the safe splashdown and return on the exact date, Friday, April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew and the Orion spacecraft completed a successful splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splash down off the coast of San Diego at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) on Friday, April 10'; R4: 'successfully completed a parachute-assisted splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)'; R3: 'splashed down ... off the coast of San Diego ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT (0007 GMT on April 11)'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time, location, and successful nature directly match across sources.

verifications.claim: The splashdown wrapped up a 10-day mission around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'approximately 10-day journey around the Moon including launch, a lunar flyby, and a safe splashdown'; R2: 'approximately 10-day journey around the Moon'; R4: 'carrying ... on an approximate 10-day mission around the Moon and back'; R9: 'nearly 10-day journey'
verifications.reasoning: All sources describe it as an approximately 10-day mission around the Moon ending with splashdown.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'SPLASHDOWN! ... successfully completed a parachute-assisted splashdown'; R3: 'a perfect bulls-eye splashdown for Integrity and its four astronauts'; R8: 'The Orion capsule landed in the Pacific Ocean upright, a picture-perfect ending'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm safe splashdown of the crew module/Orion capsule.

verifications.claim: The splashdown marked the end of a ~695,000-mile journey.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Crew is expected to travel a total of 695,081 miles'; '694,481-mile journey'; R9: 'flew 694,481 miles in total'; R3: 'flew a total of 700,237 miles'; R7: 'flew 700,237 miles'
verifications.reasoning: Sources cite distances around 694k-700k miles total journey, matching the approximate ~695,000-mile figure.

verifications.claim: Astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen were safely extracted from the capsule by recovery teams from the USS John P. Murtha.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'recovery teams will retrieve the crew using helicopters and deliver them to the USS John P. Murtha'; R4: 'The Artemis II crew ... have been safely extracted from the Orion spacecraft'; 'flown to the USS John P. Murtha'; R9: 'assisted them out of the spacecraft ... transported them via helicopter to the USS John P. Murtha'; names consistent across all
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew names and safe extraction to USS John P. Murtha by recovery teams confirmed.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed mission to the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'launched humanity back to the moon for the first time since Apollo 17 in December 1972'; R5: 'first crewed lunar mission in more than 50 years'; R9: 'first astronauts to travel to the Moon in more than half a century'; R1: 'first crewed test flight under NASA’s Artemis program'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state it as the first crewed mission to the Moon since Apollo 17 (1972), over 50 years.
